title: When Validators Don’t Trigger: A Paired Evaluation of Generate→Validate→Repair for LLM‑Generated Network Configurations
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (N = 600 task pairs) to test whether a deterministic validator–guided repair pipeline (generate→validate→repair) reduces high‑risk semantic misconfigurations relative to single‑shot LLM generation in intent→vendor‑configuration tasks. The execution used shared_initial_candidate semantics: exactly one sampled initial candidate per pair was produced and reused by both arms; the guarded arm could differ from baseline only if the deterministic validator rejected that candidate and an automated repair executed. With gpt-5-mini as the generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the validator, every shared initial candidate passed the validator in both baseline and guarded conditions (baseline = 600/600; guarded = 600/600). The paired absolute difference = 0.0 (95% bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; bootstrap resamples = 10,000, seed = 1729). No automated repairs were invoked. We report the preregistered design, clarify the scientific meaning of shared_initial_candidate semantics and the archived sampling record (temperature = null/unset does not imply deterministic sampling), present exact paired results, and discuss construct validity of validators, ceiling effects, and design recommendations for future generate→validate→repair evaluations.

sections.introduction: Intent‑driven NetOps systems translate operator intents into vendor‑specific device configurations. Prior prototype work shows feasibility of LLM‑based intent→configuration translation and commonly recommends validator‑ or tool‑augmentation (generate→validate→repair) to reduce LLM errors [1]–[3]. Important open questions remain about how to measure benefits of such augmentations under adversarial or out‑of‑distribution intents and which experimental semantics actually estimate generator‑level versus validator/repair effects. We preregistered and executed a narrowly scoped paired confirmatory study to answer the following question: Under shared_initial_candidate paired semantics (one sampled initial generation per task reused by both arms), does a deterministic validator‑guided repair pipeline reduce high‑risk semantic failures relative to accepting the single LLM generation? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired experiment executed on 600 intent→configuration pairs with archived artifacts; (2) an artifact‑grounded interpretation of the null (ceiling) outcome that arises under shared_initial_candidate semantics; and (3) concrete design recommendations for future evaluations that aim to measure validator/repair efficacy or generation‑level differences.
sections.related_work: Recent intent→configuration and NetOps systems report prototype evaluations where LLMs generate vendor configurations and system designers augment generators with validators, retrieval, or deterministic checks to reduce errors [1], [2]. Broader surveys and empirical analyses characterize hallucinations, self‑correction, and tool‑augmented agentic workflows and propose constrained decoding and neurosymbolic methods to improve structured outputs [3]–[6]. These studies are heterogeneous in datasets, validator definitions, and evaluation metrics; they motivate reproducible, workflow‑centered experiments that pair intents, vendor targets, deterministic validators, and adversarial/perturbed inputs—design decisions that this preregistration made explicit.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and experimental design: The study was preregistered as autocand-2026-01-prereg-v1 before observing outcomes. The confirmatory paired design used 600 deterministically selected task pairs (planned episodes = 1,200; completed pairs = 600). Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in high‑risk semantic failure proportions (guarded − baseline), tested with an exact McNemar two‑sided test and paired bootstrap 95% CIs (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) as declared. Execution contract and generation semantics: per the preregistered adapter contract, generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate: exactly one sampled initial generation per task was produced and reused unchanged by both baseline and guarded conditions; the guarded condition could call the deterministic validator and, if that validator failed, invoke at most one automated repair. Because of shared_initial_candidate semantics, the paired estimand measures whether the validator would have rejected the same initial candidate and whether a repair could convert that candidate into a validator‑passing configuration; it does not measure independent per‑condition generator variability. Models and validators: the declared generator was gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator was deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Implementation and accounting: the preregistration permitted up to 1,200 model calls if per‑condition independent draws were used; under shared_initial_candidate semantics the run used a single initial generation per pair and therefore model_calls_used = 600. The archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset for executed calls; null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic hosted‑model sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Inclusion/exclusion and contamination controls followed the preregistered plan (public‑source license requirement, automated provenance checks, algorithmic redaction of sensitive adversarial exemplars). Analysis and corner cases: primary analysis used the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor (exact McNemar and bootstrap CI). Note: when no discordant pairs occur (n10 = n01 = 0), bootstrap CIs and exact tests reduce to degenerate corner values; we report these exact, artifact‑backed numbers and explicitly interpret their meaning in the Results and Discussion.
sections.results: Execution accounting: The adapter executed the preregistered paired run to completion with 600 completed pairs and no model‑call failures under the shared_initial_candidate contract (planned_episode_count = 1,200; completed_episode_count = 1,200; model_calls_used = 600). Primary outcomes: the deterministic validator accepted the shared initial candidate in every episode. Exact counts: baseline_success_count = 600/600 (100%), guarded_success_count = 600/600 (100%); contingency table: n11 = 600, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI (paired_bootstrap_percentile, 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.0, 0.0]. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Repairs invoked: none—no guarded repairs executed because the validator did not reject any initial candidate. Secondary preregistered estimands (vendor‑stratified differences, repair success rate, failure‑mode breakdown) are uninformative because no validator failures occurred; archived analysis artifacts report fully passed summaries. Representative validator traces and the shared_initial_candidate reuse are archived in the execution bundle.
sections.discussion: Scientific meaning of the null (ceiling) outcome: Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded pipeline can change a paired outcome only if the deterministic validator rejects the initial candidate and an automated repair produces a validator‑passing configuration. Because the validator accepted all initial candidates, the guarded pipeline had no opportunity to demonstrate benefit; the observed null outcome therefore measures validator/repair trigger opportunities, not generator‑level improvements. Design implications: (1) Match generation semantics to the estimand: to measure generator‑level differences use independent per‑condition draws; to measure validator/repair trigger efficacy use shared_initial_candidate semantics. (2) Audit validators for construct validity (sensitivity/specificity) before confirmatory tests—overpermissive validators create ceiling effects that mask downstream protections. (3) Use adversarially stressed or harder task banks to avoid ceiling/floor effects and to elicit repair opportunities. Limitations (scope): tasks were synthetic from the preregistered deterministic task generator; only one generator (gpt-5-mini) and one validator implementation were used; the archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset which is not evidence of deterministic sampling. A planned seeded 100‑case validator audit was preregistered but not executed in the confirmatory run; validator sensitivity therefore remains an unresolved limitation and a concrete recommendation for follow‑up work.
sections.conclusion:
We executed a preregistered paired experiment (N = 600 pairs) under shared_initial_candidate semantics comparing single‑shot LLM generation and a deterministic validator‑guided repair pipeline. Both arms passed the deterministic validator in all pairs (100% baseline and guarded success), producing an observed paired difference of 0.0 (95% CI [0.0, 0.0], p = 1.0). No automated repairs were invoked. This outcome underscores that (a) generation semantics determine what a paired estimand measures (validator trigger effectiveness vs. generation differences), (b) validators should be audited to avoid ceiling effects, and (c) future experiments aiming to measure generate→validate→repair benefits should (i) use independent per‑condition generations or (ii) employ intentionally harder/adversarial task banks to create validator trigger opportunities. All preregistration, execution, validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived per the preregistered plan. References

disclosure_statement: Models, tools, and preregistration: generative calls used the declared model gpt-5-mini via the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. The deterministic validator implementation was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; tasks were produced by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. The study was preregistered as autocand-2026-01-prereg-v1 and executed under that preregistration. Autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family and approved the initial master prompt before the autonomy lock; after the lock the AI system autonomously selected the final research question, executed the preregistered experiment, performed analyses, and authored and revised the manuscript. No manual human editing of technical content, numerical results, or manuscript conclusions occurred after the autonomy lock. Master prompt reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA‑256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Generation semantics and sampling: generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate (one sampled initial generation per pair was reused by baseline and guarded); the archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset for the executed calls — null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0. Full execution manifest, raw model calls, deterministic validator traces, and analysis artifacts are archived per the preregistration.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: baseline and guarded used the identical sampled initial generation per pair; thus the paired estimand measures validator/repair trigger effectiveness, not independent generation differences.

Validator construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepted all initial candidates in this run; without an independent validator sensitivity audit this ceiling performance limits inference about the utility of tool augmentation across other task banks.

Task external validity: tasks were synthetic items generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 under the preregistered contamination and redaction rules; results may not generalize to diverse production device configurations or vendor idiosyncrasies.
Model and adapter scope: only the declared model (gpt-5-mini) and one adapter/validator instance were used; no claim of model‑class generality is made.

Sampling record: the archived model configuration records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is explicitly not evidence of deterministic sampling. Independent per‑condition sampling would be required to evaluate generator‑level effects.

Power assumptions violated: the preregistration's power calculation assumed a nonzero baseline failure rate (≈10%). The observed baseline rate was 0%, so the preregistered minimal detectable effect (5 percentage points) and power interpretation do not apply to this execution.

Planned validator audit not executed: a seeded 100‑case validator audit was preregistered but not executed as part of the archived confirmatory run; validator sensitivity therefore remains an unresolved limitation and a concrete recommendation for follow‑up work.
